Cybersecurity Study Hub

A structured learning repository built to reinforce cybersecurity knowledge across CompTIA Security+ SY0-701, Cisco Networking Academy, AI security courses, and beyond. These resources were created to reinforce active learning through structured study guides, interactive flashcards, curated references, and practical examples — demonstrating both technical knowledge and the ability to translate complex security concepts into clear, memorable learning experiences.

Whether you're a fellow learner or a hiring manager — this hub showcases curriculum development, instructional design, and technical writing applied to real certification content.

🎓 CompTIA Security+ Study Area

SY0-701 exam objectives — organized by domain with objective-level breakdowns. Click any domain to expand. For cartoon-themed analogies, visit the individual cartoon pages above.

📊 90 questions max · 90 minutes · Passing score: 750/900 📋 5 Domains · Multiple choice + Performance-based 🎯 Recommended: 2+ years IT admin experience
🔐
Domain 1
General Security Concepts
Security controls, CIA Triad, AAA, Zero Trust, cryptography, PKI, change management
12%
▾
1.1 Security Controls

Categories: Technical, Managerial, Operational, Physical. Types: Preventive, Deterrent, Detective, Corrective, Compensating, Directive.

1.2 Fundamental Concepts

CIA Triad, Non-repudiation, AAA framework, Gap analysis, Zero Trust (Control Plane & Data Plane), Physical Security, Deception Technology.

1.3 Change Management

Approval process, Ownership, Impact analysis, Backout plan, Maintenance windows, Version control, Documentation updates.

1.4 Cryptography

PKI, Symmetric/Asymmetric encryption, Key exchange, Hashing, Salting, Digital signatures, Steganography, Tokenization, Data masking, Certificates, CRL, OCSP.

Key formulas: AES (Symmetric), RSA/ECC (Asymmetric/Signatures), SHA-256 (Hashing). Remember: Public key encrypts, Private key decrypts (asymmetric).

⚡
Domain 2 · Largest threat domain
Threats, Vulnerabilities & Mitigations
Threat actors, malware, social engineering, vulnerabilities, IoC, hardening
22%
▾
2.1 Threat Actors

Nation-state, Unskilled attacker, Hacktivist, Insider threat, Organized crime, Shadow IT. Attributes: internal/external, resources, sophistication.

2.2 Attack Vectors

Message-based (email, SMS, IM), Image/file-based, Voice, Removable devices, Vulnerable software, Unsecure networks, Supply chain, Social engineering (Phishing, Vishing, Smishing, Typosquatting).

2.3 Vulnerabilities

Buffer overflow, Race conditions (TOC/TOU), SQLi, XSS, Firmware, VM escape, Cloud-specific, Zero-day, Misconfiguration, Mobile (sideloading, jailbreaking).

2.4–2.5 IoC & Mitigations

Account lockout, Impossible travel, Missing logs. Mitigations: Segmentation, ACLs, Allow lists, Patching, Encryption, Least privilege, Hardening techniques.

🃏 Full D2 Flashcards ⌚ Ben 10 Threat Actors 🍩 Simpsons Villains
🏗️
Domain 3
Security Architecture
Cloud models, firewalls, VPN, segmentation, data protection, resilience & recovery
18%
▾
3.1 Architecture Models

Cloud (IaaS/PaaS/SaaS), IaC, Serverless, Microservices, SDN, Containerization, Virtualization, IoT, SCADA/ICS, RTOS, Embedded systems, High availability.

3.2 Infrastructure Security

Device placement, Security zones, Fail-open/closed, Jump server, IPS/IDS, Load balancer, Port security (802.1X/EAP), WAF, UTM, NGFW, VPN, TLS, IPSec, SD-WAN, SASE.

3.3 Data Protection

Data types & classifications, Data at rest/in transit/in use, Data sovereignty, Encryption, Hashing, Masking, Tokenization, Segmentation, Geographic restrictions.

3.4 Resilience & Recovery

Hot/Warm/Cold sites, Geographic dispersion, Multi-cloud, Capacity planning, Tabletop exercises, Backups (onsite/offsite, snapshots, replication), Generators, UPS.

Key metrics: RTO (how fast to restore) · RPO (how much data loss acceptable) · MTTR (avg repair time) · MTBF (avg time between failures)
🃏 Full D3 Flashcards 🌊 Avatar Architecture 👻 Danny Phantom Segmentation
🔍
Domain 4 · Largest domain on exam
Security Operations
Incident response, forensics, IAM, SIEM/SOAR, vulnerability management, automation
28%
▾
4.1–4.2 Security Techniques & Assets

Secure baselines, Hardening (mobile, workstations, routers, servers, IoT), MDM (BYOD/COPE/CYOD), WPA3, Application security, Asset lifecycle management.

4.3–4.4 Vulnerability & Monitoring

Vulnerability scanning, CVSS, CVE, Penetration testing, Bug bounty. SIEM, SOAR, Log aggregation, Alert tuning, DLP, NetFlow, EDR/XDR.

4.6 Identity & Access Management

Provisioning, MFA (biometrics, tokens, keys), SSO (LDAP, OAuth, SAML), RBAC, ABAC, DAC, MAC, PAM (JIT, password vaulting, ephemeral credentials).

4.8–4.9 IR & Forensics

IR Lifecycle: Preparation → Detection → Analysis → Containment → Eradication → Recovery → Lessons Learned. Chain of custody, Order of volatility, Legal hold, E-discovery.

Critical IR rule: Always CONTAIN before you ERADICATE — stopping spread takes priority over cleanup.
🃏 Full D4 Flashcards 🐕 Scooby-Doo IR Lifecycle 🤖 Futurama IAM & Ports
📋
Domain 5
Security Program Management & Oversight
Governance, risk management, compliance, third-party risk, audits, security awareness
20%
▾
5.1 Security Governance

Policies (AUP, BCP, IR, SDLC, change management), Standards, Procedures, External considerations (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS), Governance structures, Data roles (Owner/Controller/Processor/Custodian).

5.2 Risk Management

Risk identification, Qualitative vs quantitative analysis, SLE = AV × EF, ALE = SLE × ARO, Risk register, Risk appetite (expansionary/neutral/conservative), Strategies: Transfer/Accept/Avoid/Mitigate.

5.3 Third-Party Risk

Vendor assessment, Right-to-audit, Supply chain analysis, Due diligence. Agreements: SLA, MOU, MOA, NDA, MSA, SOW, BPA.

5.4–5.6 Compliance & Awareness

Compliance monitoring, Privacy (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS), Attestation, Internal/external audits, Penetration testing types, Phishing campaigns, Security awareness training.

Critical formulas: SLE = AV × EF  ·  ALE = SLE × ARO  ·  RTO = how fast to restore  ·  RPO = how much data loss is acceptable

🧠 How the Leitner System Works

Cards you miss return to Box 1 (reviewed every session). Cards you know advance to higher boxes reviewed less often — all the way to Box 5 (Mastered). Your brain gets more practice exactly where it needs it most, automatically. Portfolio Rationale

More Than a Study Guide

This platform was intentionally designed to demonstrate applied competencies in instructional design, governance, and human-centered learning — not just technical knowledge.

🎓

ADDIE Framework

Every page on this hub follows the ADDIE instructional design model. Learner needs were analyzed against CompTIA SY0-701 exam objectives; content was designed around schema activation and character-to-concept mapping; interactive elements (flashcards, quizzes, games) were developed to support spaced repetition and retrieval practice; the site is deployed via GitHub Pages for open access; and ongoing revisions reflect continuous evaluation of what works for retention.

🛡️

GRC Alignment

The curriculum is scoped directly to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and CompTIA SY0-701 domain objectives, with dedicated coverage of Governance, Risk, and Compliance concepts including risk registers, policy frameworks, incident response procedures, and audit readiness. Content organization mirrors how security awareness training is structured in enterprise environments.

🤖

AI-Assisted Development

This platform was built entirely through human-led, AI-assisted development — using Claude to generate, iterate, and refine every component from the ground up. The result demonstrates not just what was learned, but proficiency in leveraging modern AI tools to produce professional-grade instructional content, interactive applications, and technical documentation at speed.

Instructional Design Curriculum Development Technical Writing Knowledge Management GRC Frameworks Security Awareness Training UDL Principles AI-Assisted Development
